exposure: attempt at vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC)
cohort: The study included 60 pregnant women with a previous cesarean section who attempted vaginal birth.
finding: Successful vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) was achieved in 85% of cases and was associated with less maternal and perinatal morbidity and shorter hospital stays compared to emergency C-sections following a failed VBAC attempt.
mod_finding: Successful VBAC was associated with lower maternal and perinatal morbidity and shorter hospital stays compared to emergency C-sections performed after attempted VBAC.
